PullRequest.Title: Remove featured sections from the customizations modal
PullRequest.Body: ## Summary Removes the Featured sections from the Plugins and MCP Servers pages of the customizations modal. - Delete the featured-section rendering code and dedicated CSS. - Remove the proposed experimental setting, Stable/Insiders gates, and their product-service dependencies. - Keep Installed and Available sections, marketplace browsing, and search intact. - Remove obsolete featured-toggle fixtures and refresh the six changed blocks-ci screenshot hashes using the Linux CI output. ## Validation - 46 targeted plugin/MCP unit tests passed. - 34 affected component fixtures rendered successfully in light and dark themes, including all 10 variants that failed in CI. - Targeted ESLint and diff whitespace checks passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Plugins page in the customizations modal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The installed/available shell renders synchronously; the marketplace snapshot request is asynchronous and only gates population of Available results, not initial page display. The diff removes the Featured section from both the initial and post-fetch render paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch each configured plugin marketplace through raw GitHub HTTP or ensure a cloned repository and read manifests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one snapshot fetch per visible widget initialization, fanning out once per deduplicated configured marketplace; warm GitHub entries can be served from the TTL cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshot request populated both Featured and Available; after the diff the same single request populates Available only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial-render critical path, but completion is required to populate Available marketplace cards.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed and remote plugin counts plus the deduplicated marketplace plugin result across configured marketplaces. The Available list remains virtualized; the removed Featured work was capped at three rendered entries but also performed an extra full marketplace filter/sort pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One widget snapshot request is admitted by the uninitialized/loading state guard. Configured marketplace references are fetched concurrently with Promise.all in the service; repeated home renders do not start another snapshot request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The widget snapshot changes from uninitialized to loading to loaded/failed and is reused for the widget lifetime. GitHub marketplace sources use a TTL cache; cold sources may perform HTTP or clone-backed reads, while warm sources return cached entries. None of these cache rules changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the visibility guard, snapshot state machine, service fan-out, and removed render call are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Marketplace count and cold-source latency vary by configuration, but request cardinality and scheduling are unchanged; rendering work is reduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The change removes duplicate card/filter/layout work and does not add, move, or multiply the marketplace boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the MCP Servers page in the customizations modal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The installed/available shell renders first; an asynchronous first-page gallery query populates Available. The diff removes the Featured section from every home render without changing query scheduling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the MCP gallery manifest if needed and query the registry for the first page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One guarded first-page request on cold visible-home entry; subsequent home renders reuse gallerySnapshotServers unless the manifest changes or an explicit refresh path runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same gallery query fed both Featured and Available sections; after the diff it feeds Available only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the first shell render but required for Available results.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed MCP entries and the first gallery page after installed-server deduplication. Available remains virtualized; the removed Featured section duplicated at most three entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The visibility, access, loading, failure, and empty-snapshot guard admits one initial gallery query. A cancellation token replaces stale requests; no new concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first page is retained in gallerySnapshotServers for the widget lifetime and refreshed only on manifest changes or explicit paths. Manifest/service caching behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: query guard, cancellation ownership, snapshot retention, and removed rendering are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry response size and latency vary, but the diff leaves request count, pagination, cancellation, and cache lifetime unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. DOM creation and layout are reduced while all expensive boundary behavior remains unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse or search plugin and MCP marketplaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Debounced search or explicit browse queries remain the only boundary-dependent work before remote results appear. The deleted Featured render methods are not used on browse/search result surfaces.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch plugin marketplace definitions for browse/search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical request per explicit browse entry or settled search, with unchanged per-marketplace service fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical request and cancellation paths before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before marketplace search/browse results are shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the MCP gallery registry for settled search text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per settled query after debounce, replacing stale requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical request and cancellation paths before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for authoritative remote search results; cached snapshot filtering can provide interim local matches.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Search frequency after 400 ms debouncing and first-page/result collection size after installed-item filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each widget cancels/replaces stale requests; plugin marketplace sources fan out by deduplicated marketplace, while MCP uses one registry query per effective debounced search.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Plugin source caches and MCP manifest state are unchanged. Home snapshots may supply immediate local filtering, and authoritative search requests remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: browse/search branches bypass the deleted home-only sections and their boundary calls are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual user typing cadence and source latency vary, but no changed hunk reaches these scheduling paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Search and browse cardinality, caching, and concurrency are unaffected.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render plugin catalog component screenshot fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new setVisible(true) synchronously starts refresh and an asynchronous snapshot fetch before fixture capture; the helper already waits fixed 100/600 ms plus 200 ms, so this in-memory fetch does not add an external wait. It is needed to render the Available fixture data after Featured removal.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Five helper variants, each rendered in light and dark themes, over a fixed marketplacePlugins fixture array.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The home variants start one snapshot promise. Browse/search variants can also start their existing explicit query path, but both fake service calls resolve immediately from memory and are bounded per fixture.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each fixture constructs a fresh widget and snapshot; there is no cross-fixture cache. The fake marketplace service returns the static array directly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the injected IPluginMarketplaceService implementation is directly visible and its fetch method only returns marketplacePlugins.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Fixture runner scheduling can vary, but there is no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation behind the changed visibility call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added work is test-only, bounded, in-memory, and fits inside pre-existing fixed screenshot waits.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and all diff pages. The product changes remove bounded duplicate rendering and related CSS; marketplace fetch, cache, debounce, cancellation, and concurrency behavior remain unchanged. The sole added executable line is fixture-only visibility setup backed by an in-memory mock. No actionable performance finding or qualifying shipped-regression fix was established.
